user_symptom: Camera 'Cam 1' authorization required (password prompt loops); Video failed (Check username and password)
root_cause: majestic ONVIF WSSE parser only matches namespace-PREFIXED <wsse:Security>/<wsse:UsernameToken>; tinyCam sends the semantically-identical UNPREFIXED default-namespace form <Security xmlns=...>, so majestic never finds the UsernameToken and treats every request as unauthenticated.
tinycam_auth_mode: WSSE UsernameToken PasswordDigest, unprefixed default namespace; retried ~35x, never falls back to PasswordText or HTTP Basic
why_pr357_did_not_help: PR #357 / 9015d295 added a PRE_AUTH allowlist and challenge emission. tinyCam's GetDeviceInformation is not a PRE_AUTH op, and the WSSE namespace-parsing limitation is untouched by that PR. This camera's build (c5bf196, Aug 14) also predates the Aug-20 fix.
two_independent_blockers_for_tinycam: WSSE namespace prefix: majestic must accept unprefixed <Security xmlns=...> (resolve by namespace URI, not literal prefix)
PasswordDigest verification requires onvif.password (cleartext); cannot be checked against hashed /etc/shadow
fix_location_majestic: src/onvif/wsse.c find_username_token (mxml prefix resolution); per kaeru onvif-auth-regression node
workaround_none_sufficient: Setting onvif.password alone does NOT fix tinyCam (namespace bug still rejects it); both fixes are required. Confirmed live: with onvif.password=123456 set, tinyCam still failed.
capture_method: Android emulator (KVM) driving tinyCam via adb; host-side logging TCP relay (harness/relay.py) since emulator -tcpdump does not capture the slirp-NAT'd camera path
